0231ec7573a2.title: Simulation, Sim to Real (Internship Program)
0231ec7573a2.description_html:
FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field. FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field.

About the Role

Join Field AI’s Simulation team for a 12-week internship building tools that connect real-world robot deployments with autonomy development. You’ll work alongside simulation and autonomy engineers on a scoped project in simulation tooling, sensor fidelity, real-to-sim workflows, or autonomy evaluation, with opportunities to validate your work against real robot data.

What You'll Get To Do

Work with a mentor to define and deliver a focused simulation project over 12 weeks.

Develop or improve robotics simulation tools using Python and/or C++.

Help evaluate and improve simulation fidelity in an area such as sensor modeling, timing, robot behavior, or environment representation.

Build tools for scenario execution, log replay, regression testing, metrics, or visualization.

Use field logs, reconstructed environments, or real-world failure cases to create reproducible simulation scenarios.

Collaborate with simulation and autonomy engineers to investigate differences between simulated and real robot behavior.

Document your approach and share your results through a final demo and technical handoff.

Your project will focus on a subset of these areas, based on your interests, experience, and team priorities.

What You Have

Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.

Programming experience in Python and/or C++ through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects.

Foundational knowledge in one or more areas such as robotics, simulation, computer graphics, physics, or software engineering.

Experience building and debugging software, including familiarity with Git and Linux.

Interest in understanding how sensing, timing, physics, and environments affect robot behavior.

A collaborative mindset, curiosity, and willingness to learn unfamiliar tools.

Availability for a 12-week internship.

What Will Set You Apart

Hands-on experience with Isaac Sim, Gazebo, MuJoCo, Unity, Unreal, or another simulation platform.

Familiarity with ROS2, including sensor messages, coordinate transforms, or recorded robot data.

Experience working with robot or environment assets such as URDF, USD, meshes, or point clouds.

Projects involving sensor simulation, physics modeling, 3D reconstruction, or procedural environment generation.

Experience with automated testing, CI workflows, batch simulation, or data analysis and visualization.

Experience using real robot data to evaluate simulation accuracy or autonomy performance.

Participation in robotics research, student teams, competitions, or open-source projects.

Our salary range is generous and we consider each individual’s background and experience when determining final compensation. Base pay may vary based on role scope, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the Irvine, California market.   Why Join FieldAI in Irvine? In Irvine, you will work where the robots are. Our local team builds and tests systems on real hardware with real sensors, then ships them to operate in unstructured, previously unknown environments around the world. We are solving one of robotics’ hardest challenges: reliable deployment outside the lab. Our Field Foundational Models™ raise the bar for perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, with an emphasis on explainability and safety for real-world use. You will collaborate with a world-class team that thrives on creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. We bring deep experience from organizations such as DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX, along with a track record of field deployments and strong performance in DARPA challenge segments.   Be Part of the Next Robotics Revolution We are looking for builders who want their work to leave the whiteboard and show up on robots. If you enjoy tackling tough, uncharted questions and working across disciplines, you will find your people here. Our teams span AI, software, robotics engineering, product, field deployment, and technical communication, all focused on shipping systems that perform in the real world.   Our headquarters is in Irvine, and we partner closely with teams there as well as colleagues across the US and around the world. Join us in Southern California and help define what dependable, field-ready autonomy looks like.   We value diverse perspectives and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We evaluate candidates and employees based on merit, qualifications, and performance, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

02528414746f.title: Systems Engineer Intern - St. Pete Site
02528414746f.title_raw: Systems Engineer Intern - St. Pete Site
02528414746f.description_html:
Acron Aviation is seeking motivated and innovative Systems Engineering Interns to join our engineering team in St. Petersburg, Florida.This full-time, onsite internship is anticipated to run May through August and provides an opportunity to apply classroom knowledge in a professional engineering environment. You will work alongside experienced systems engineers and contribute to projects supporting the development, integration, verification, certification, and sustainment of aerospace recorder products and related technologies.Depending on your assigned team and project, you may gain experience in systems development, requirements analysis, product design, system integration, verification and validation, environmental testing, problem investigation, and technical documentation. Intern assignments will be aligned with current business and program needs while providing exposure to real-world aerospace systems engineering practices and the development of safety-critical aviation products. Acron Aviation is seeking motivated and innovative Systems Engineering Interns to join our engineering team in St. Petersburg, Florida.This full-time, onsite internship is anticipated to run May through August and provides an opportunity to apply classroom knowledge in a professional engineering environment. You will work alongside experienced systems engineers and contribute to projects supporting the development, integration, verification, certification, and sustainment of aerospace recorder products and related technologies.Depending on your assigned team and project, you may gain experience in systems development, requirements analysis, product design, system integration, verification and validation, environmental testing, problem investigation, and technical documentation. Intern assignments will be aligned with current business and program needs while providing exposure to real-world aerospace systems engineering practices and the development of safety-critical aviation products.

What You Will Do

Work under the guidance of experienced systems engineers and technical team members supporting recorder products and related aerospace systems. Support development and review of system requirements, specifications, interface definitions, and design documentation. Assist with systems analysis, modeling, and product development activities. Help translate customer, regulatory, certification, and program requirements into clear and testable system requirements. Develop or update test procedures, test scripts, verification plans, and validation documentation. Execute functional, environmental, integration, and system-level testing under engineering guidance. Analyze test results and document findings, anomalies, and recommendations. Support product integration, verification, validation, regression testing, and issue reproduction activities. Participate in test readiness reviews and help ensure test equipment, configurations, and procedures are prepared for execution. Assist in investigating defects, failures, and unexpected product behavior. Support root cause analysis and corrective action activities. Participate in design reviews, technical discussions, project meetings, and engineering peer reviews. Support preparation and maintenance of engineering documentation, requirements traceability, and configuration-controlled artifacts. Assist with configuration management and product lifecycle activities. Collaborate with Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Quality, Certification, and Program Engineering teams. Support qualification, environmental, laboratory, and certification testing activities. Identify opportunities to improve testing efficiency, automation, documentation quality, and engineering processes. Perform other systems engineering assignments aligned with your academic background and the needs of the assigned team. This position may require access to information, technology, software, or hardware that is subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations. To comply with these requirements, applicants must qualify as a US Person.

Required Qualifications

Currently enrolled in an accredited bachelor’s or master’s degree program in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline. Expected to have completed at least two years of undergraduate study before the internship begins. Foundational understanding of engineering development, requirements, testing, debugging, and problem-solving concepts. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills. Ability to follow detailed technical procedures and engineering processes. Ability to clearly communicate work status, questions, findings, and potential issues. Ability to organize technical information and document results accurately. Effective verbal communication, technical writing, and presentation skills. Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary engineering environment. Ability to take direction, ask questions when needed, and complete assigned work with an appropriate level of independence. Ability to work full-time and onsite at the assigned Acron Aviation location for the duration of the internship.

Preferred Qualifications

Systems engineering principles and lifecycle processes Requirements development, allocation, and traceability System architecture and interface definition Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) Product verification, validation, and certification activities System integration and troubleshooting Development and execution of test procedures and test plans Environmental, qualification, or reliability testing Data analysis and interpretation Configuration management and change control Defect investigation and root cause analysis Test automation or scripting Aerospace electronics, avionics, or embedded systems Flight data recorders, cockpit voice recorders, or aircraft data acquisition systems Safety-critical or regulated product development environments DO-178, DO-254, ARINC, FAA, EASA, or other aerospace industry standards and processes Aerospace, aviation, defense, or other highly regulated industries   Equal Opportunity StatementAcron Aviation is proud to be an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to treating all employees and applicants with respect and dignity and to maintaining a workplace free from unlawful discrimination. All applicants will be considered for employment regardless of race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, or other related medical conditions), gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, disability, genetic information, citizenship status, or any other legally protected characteristic. Additional Information:Acron Aviation maintains a drug-free workplace and conducts pre-employment substance abuse testing and background checks, where allowed by law. Acron Aviation is an E-Verify employer
